subject: Air-gapped networking and immutable image cycle
messages:
From: Megan Liu <megan@cobaltindustrial.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Air-gapped deployment: network boundary and image cycle questions

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the quick intro call last week. As we begin scoping our on-prem / VPC-islanded deployment I want to capture a few concrete requirements from our side so your team can confirm the workflow we need to support. High-level: we are an industrial control customer — no egress, strictly controlled ingress windows, and an auditable image lifecycle.

Questions:
- Network: do you support a single DMZ transfer appliance pattern (one-way courier) vs push-pull? Any recommended firewall/NAT rules or port lists for the on-site ingress host?
- Image artifacts: what formats do you accept (OCI tar, signed tar.gz, container image plus manifest)? We require a detached signature and a signer chain.
- Keying: can Redwood integrate with customer HSM for root signing, or do you provide a signer/operator key ceremony model?
- Update cadence & rollback: we need an agreed acceptance window, automated rollback criteria, and a documented test activation (no-production) step.

Can you send a short architecture sketch and a proposed acceptance/rollback playbook we can review before scheduling an on-site key ceremony? We are targeting a maintenance window the week of Dec 6.

Thanks,
Megan Liu
Infrastructure Lead
Cobalt Industrial
ops@cobaltindustrial.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan@cobaltindustrial.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:05:23 -0800
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment: network boundary and image cycle questions

Megan — thanks, clear requirements. Attached is a first-pass network sketch and a short runbook (network-diagram-draft.pdf). Summary answers below; I kept items concise so we can iterate quickly: 

- Transfer pattern: we support both patterns but recommend the one-way courier model (customer-supplied transfer appliance inside DMZ) for strict no-egress environments. The appliance pulls nothing from the internet; we ship a signed, immutable bundle which your operator imports via the appliance USB/courier.
- Firewall/ports: for the sealed mode there are no outbound ports required. If you enable remote attestation, only an internal management control plane port (443) to a private endpoint is optionally opened via an egress jump; otherwise 0 outbound ports. In the hybrid VPC-onprem option we document specific CIDR and port lists — see attached.
- Artifact format & signing: we accept an OCI-style bundle (tar.gz) plus a detached high-entropy signature (Ed25519 or RSA-PSS). We produce a manifest.json with checksums; manifest is signed by Redwood’s operator keys. Your security team may replace the operator signature with a customer HSM-signed root — we support importing customer root certs into the verification chain.
- Key ceremony: Redwood offers two models: 1) Redwood-managed operator signing with quarterly key rotation and an auditable KMS/HSM-stored key; 2) Customer-hosted signing where we provide tooling and a documented multi-party key ceremony (operator + customer witness). Both support a notarized signature chain and embedded provenance metadata.
- Acceptance & rollback: propose a 72-hour acceptance window with staged activation (staging node -> pilot nodes -> full). Automated health checks (process liveness, sample inference responses, and checksum verification) should be run; failure at any stage triggers automatic rollback to previous immutable image and an operator alert. Detailed rollback decision tree in the draft runbook.

Next steps: can Marissa (security) confirm whether Cobalt requires customer-hosted signing or if Redwood-managed is acceptable? If customer-hosted, we’ll propose a key ceremony script and an on-site date. I can also provide a pre-filled manifest template and a sample signed bundle you can test in an isolated lab.

Attachment: network-diagram-draft.pdf (1.4MB)

Regards,
Connor O'Brien

Megan — looping in some security/ops details and the signed manifest stub for your team to verify.

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 11:05 AM Connor O\u2019Brien wrote:
> - Artifact format & signing: we accept an OCI-style bundle (tar.gz) plus a detached high-entropy signature (Ed25519 or RSA-PSS).

A few operational items to lock down before we book the on-site key ceremony: 
1) Signer ownership & audit: If you choose customer-hosted signing, we require a 3-party witness model (Cobalt operator, Redwood operator, and a third independent witness). Audits are recorded to an append-only ledger (SHA256 merkle-root logged).
2) Manifest contents: manifest must include image checksum, ML model sha256, build-recipe id, provenance notes, and a timestamp. Weve attached a manifest stub signed by Redwood for format validation.
3) Acceptance tests: list of gating tests we run during the acceptance window (see bullets below). Results are pushed to a local acceptance artifact store; no external egress is allowed.

Gating tests (summary):
- Binary & checksum validation (manifest-driven)
- Deterministic inference smoke tests (preconfigured prompt set)
- Security posture verification (no outbound sockets, correct file permissions)
- Resource soak (72h minimum on pilot node)

Rollback decision points (summary):
- Immediate rollback if checksum mismatch, process crash loop, or anomalous inference results beyond configured tolerance.
- Controlled rollback for performance regressions with manual approval.

Attachment: airgap-image-manifest-v3.json.sig (detached signature, 4KB)

Links:
- Key ceremony checklist: https://drive.redwood.com/airgap/COB-1123/plan-draft
- DocuSign for access attest: https://docusign.net/sign/cobalt-airgap-key-ceremony

Can you confirm whether Cobalt needs Redwood to hold operator signing keys for initial onboard or if youd prefer immediate customer-hosted HSM signing? Once you confirm well lock a date for the ceremony and provide a courier checklist for the sealed bundle.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
